title: Unexpected autotiling result with two terrain sets
body: ### Tested versions Tested with a few versions I had lying around: - Godot_v4.5.1-stable_mono_linux_x86_64 - Godot_v4.5-stable_mono_linux_x86_64 - Godot_v4.3-stable_linux.x86_64 ### System information Linux (Ubuntu) ### Issue description In my game I wanted to have tiles with some mossy terrain, so I drew a tilemap and made it work with 3x3 autotiling. I then wanted to add plants as decorations. I figured I'd add the plants as another terrain (instead of, say, Sprite2D) because my goal is to have the ceiling tile automatically adjust to the plant that hangs from it. Below is my expected result, with a tileset setup like so: The top 4 tiles work, and they're just the usual autotiles. Then I want one tile that gets picked when there's a plant below it, and one plant tile that can hang below that tile. When I draw it, there's unfortunately inconsistent results: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e6f2500d-2bf3-4fba-a241-10e960c5da66 I picked terrain 0 first, drawing the ground tiles. I then expect to be able to draw with terrain 1 (the plants) and have the ceiling tile adjust. The ceiling tile _does_ adjust, so something is happening, but it adjusts as if I had drawn another ground tile below it, not a plant. As you can see in the last step in the video, if I use terrain 1 (plants) to draw over the ceiling tile, it paints the correct tile. ### Steps to reproduce - set up a tilemap as in screenshot above - paint ground tiles vertically - paint one plant - the ceiling tile adjusts to an incorrect tile ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [autotiling-with-different-terrains-mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23140436/autotiling-with-different-terrains-mrp.zip)
